---
title: "Principles"
---

This page will be generated from the rule files under `rules/`: one row per
rule with its plain-language condition, its classical source (text, chapter
and verse), the studies that use it, and whether it has passed its
reference-chart tests.

The rules catalogue is being built. Until it is published, the principles each
study uses are described in that study's paper (see the Studies menu).

To propose a principle for testing, see [Contribute](contribute.qmd).

## Where the rules come from

Each rule names its root: a classical text with chapter and verse and the
translation used, a named practitioner's dated post, video or article, or a
published study. Rules stated by today's practitioners sit beside the
classical ones, labelled experimental, so the field's living practice can be
tested as openly as its texts, and where practitioners disagree both sides are
kept. The policy, the list of sources and the claims still waiting for a
traceable source are in
[Sources of rule development](https://github.com/astro-fusion/astro_research-white-paper/blob/main/docs/research/SOURCES_OF_RULE_DEVELOPMENT.md).
